contexts.text: Tubal-Cain the instructor of every artificer in brass and iron () = the doctrine of natural good and truth.
Iron, in the Word = natural truth. Illustrated.
For iron I will bring silver () = for natural truth spiritual truth... For stones iron = for sensuous truth natural truth. AC 1551:2. AC 6432:2.
A land whose stones are iron ()... Iron = natural or rational truth.
That iron = natural truth. Further illustrated.
Strength is attributed to Truth... and therefore it is predicated of iron, by which is signified Truth, or the truth of faith, which breaks up and bruises. Illustrated.
They compared... the lower Spiritual to iron.

Stones... upon which iron has been moved (; ) = things artificial, and thus the invented things of worship, that is, which are from proprium... For the same reason, iron was not moved upon the stones of the Temple ().
The Most Ancients compared... lower truths to iron. Hence was derived (the name)... Iron Age. Defined.
His shoe iron () = natural truth. AC 2162:14.
The truths of natural things are signified by the iron (in the feet of the statute).
The Iron Age then began, and as there was then no longer correspondence, Heaven was closed...
By the feet which were iron and clay () was represented the fourth state of the Church, which was one of natural truth, which is the iron.
Iron () = natural truth.
Bright iron () = natural truth, which is the first.
An iron rod () = the power of spiritual truth in natural; for all natural truth in which there is spiritual truth has power. Iron = natural truth. Illustrated.
Iron () = natural truth, which is strong to destroy falsities.
Under Tool, see this reference.
Iron, in the opposite sense, = falsity in the natural man. References.
The iron of an axe falling from its wood () = truth separated from good.
The fourth (state of the Church) is signified by the iron, which is natural truth.

As the fourth state was the truth of faith, it is said that its thighs were of iron; and as the last state was truth, which is called of faith, without good, it is said that its feet were as to a part of iron, and as to a part of clay. AC 10050:end.
Bright iron = ultimate celestial truth.

But when not even natural good (brass) remained with the man of the Church, the Lord came into the world... and then a fourth Church began, which is called Christian... But as the man of this Church has also extinguished the good (of love and charity), he cannot be informed by any influx or by illustration (from the ), but only concerning some truths, which, however, do not cohere with good. Hence these times are what are called iron; for iron = truth in the ultimate of order; but when the truth is such, it is of the quality described in .
Iron, from which the last Age is called, = hard truth without good.
That they had breastplates like breastplates of iron () = the argumentations from fallacies by which they fight and are strong. AR 436.
As an iron wall this dogma...

He shall rule them with an iron rod () = by means of truths from the sense of the letter... and at the same time by means of rational things from natural lumen... By iron is signified natural truth, consequently the natural sense of the Word, and at the same time the natural lumen of man. The power of truth consists in these two things.
For iron, from its hardness, = what is strong.
By a vessel of iron () is signified what is scientific from natural truth.
Brass = natural good, and thence iron = natural truth. Illustrated.
Like bottles filled with filings of iron commingled with sulphureous powder... TCR 113:2. TCR 116:end.

An axe, in these places, = falsity from Own intelligence. The reason is, that by iron is signified truth in ultimates, which is called sensuous truth, and which, when separated from rational and spiritual truth, is turned into falsity. Illustrated.
The metals which appear in the Spiritual World correspond... the iron to the truths of faith.
(The people who had lived in the Iron Age, visited and Described.)
(The people who lived in the Age of iron mixed with clay, visited and Described.)

Nor in their feet is there anything of pure iron; but in their heads there is iron mixed with clay, in their breasts there are both mixed with brass, in their loins there are both mixed with silver, and in their feet they are mixed with gold.
The ground there consisted of a mixture of sulphur, filings of iron, and miry clay.
Like the (sound of) iron shoes on a stone pavement.
The last age was called the Iron one, because there then reigned only truth without good; and when this reigns, falsity also reigns.
Iron = the truth of the Natural.
The iron of which a sword is made = truth in ultimates.
He shall rule them with an iron rod = that He will chastise evils by the truths which are in the natural man... Iron = the truths in the natural man, which chastise. AE 176:4.

The reason iron = truths in the natural man, is that metals... from their correspondence = spiritual and celestial things... copper or brass = the good of the external or natural man; iron, its truth...
The Iron Age was so called from the descendants of these, who were in natural truth alone without good. Natural truth is truth in the memory, and not in the life.
A pillar of iron () = truth supporting it.
Iron () = truth without good.
I will make thine horn iron () = Divine truth strong and powerful.
Iron () = spiritual natural truth.
Iron = falsity.
Iron = natural truth. AE 438:5.
A hammer has a like signification to iron, which = truth in ultimates and the truth of faith.
His soul came into the iron () = that it was so because there was no longer natural truth, but falsity.

The things which are of the sense of the letter... are signified by brass, tin, iron, and lead (), because by these things are signified the goods and truths of the natural man, for which man are those things of the Word which are contained in the sense of its letter.
The natural man as to what is scientific is signified by a furnace of iron (Illustrated.) A furnace = the natural man; and iron = what is scientific; here, a false Scientific...
It had great teeth of iron () = hard falsities from the sensuous man against the truths and goods of the Church.
Breastplates like iron breastplates = the persuasions with which they gird themselves for combats, against which the rational truths of the spiritual man do not avail.

Iron = truth in ultimates, and also falsity there; and at the same time what is hard and persuasive therein, which causes the falsity to be so hard that the truths opposed to it rebound as if they were of no account or strength.

By a graver, a hammer, and an axe; and, in general, by iron; is signified truth in its ultimate; and this is especially falsified from the proprium of man; for this truth is like the truth of the sense of the letter...
To fabricate iron with the tongs... () = to hatch falsities...
Iron = truth in ultimates.
Vessels of brass and iron () = the Knowledges of natural good and truth...
Such (falsified and adulterated) truth is signified by the pan of iron which he was to set for a wall between himself and the city ()...

Who shall pasture all nations with an iron rod () = which by the power of natural truth from spiritual shall argue with and convince those who are in falsities and evils, and are yet in the Church where the Word is.

Iron = truth in the natural man... And all the power which is possessed by the truths in the natural man is from the influx of truth and good from the spiritual man; that is, from the influx of Divine truth from the Lord through the spiritual man into the natural.
That the last state of that Church would be devoid of all good of love and of all wisdom, is signified by the toes being part iron, and part clay...
The metal iron corresponds to natural truth.
Of brass and iron () = natural goods and truths also profaned.
